description: This course covers AI techniques for detecting and mitigating cyber threats, including supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms such as Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, and Autoencoders; deep learning methods like CNNs and RNNs for intrusion detection; NLP for analyzing phishing emails and malware metadata; and AI-driven security tools like IBM QRadar and Darktrace. It also explores ethical AI in cybersecurity, standard compliance frameworks such as NIST SP 800-171, and AI-driven incident response strategies using tools like Splunk and ELK Stack.

clos.text: Define key AI concepts and their applications in cybersecurity, including machine learning models, neural networks, and natural language processing.
Describe the architecture and functionality of AI-driven cybersecurity tools like IBM QRadar and Darktrace.
Explain the principles of ethical AI in cybersecurity, including bias mitigation and compliance with NIST SP 800-171.
Apply AI algorithms such as Random Forests and CNNs to real-world cybersecurity datasets for threat detection and classification.
Implement AI-based incident response workflows using tools like Splunk and ELK Stack for automated threat mitigation.
